gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 13?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 13 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble guidance from the German Weather Service (DWD) and ECMWF positions Munich’s August 13 maximum near 31 °C, driving the 60 % market-implied probability for that outcome. A stable high-pressure ridge is advecting warmer air from the southwest, supporting afternoon peaks of 30–32 °C under mostly clear skies and light winds, as indicated by forecast soundings. This represents a modest positive anomaly relative to the August climatological mean daily maximum of 24–26 °C. Minor model spread between 30 °C and 32 °C stems primarily from small differences in boundary-layer moisture and any residual cloud timing, with the next DWD update expected to narrow the precise peak within the 30–32 °C window.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent high pressure over the UK and a southerly flow of warm continental air are sustaining elevated temperatures into mid-August, with ensemble forecasts from the Met Office and ECMWF converging on a London maximum of 31–34°C for August 14.** Clear skies and light winds are expected to maximize daytime insolation, while the urban heat island effect in central London can add 1–2°C relative to surrounding areas. 

The heatwave, already peaking near 35–37°C on August 13 across parts of southern England under an amber Met Office warning, is forecast to ease only modestly on Friday as a weak front approaches from the northwest. Model spreads remain narrow around 32–33°C, reflecting limited uncertainty in the short-range guidance and explaining why these outcomes dominate trader positioning at 45% and 29.5% respectively. A faster or stronger cooling trend could shift probability toward 31°C or lower, while any delay in the frontal passage would favor 34°C.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 12 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the LaGuardia Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/ny/new-york-city/KLGA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service short-range guidance and real-time observations have anchored the August 12 daily maximum at LaGuardia Airport firmly in the upper 80s, driving the 99.8% market-implied probability for the 86–87°F bin. Mid-August climatology in New York City centers near 83°F, but persistent clear skies, light winds, and stable boundary-layer conditions have supported modest daytime warming without the moisture or instability needed to reach 90°F. Ensemble model consensus shows narrow spread, with resolution tied to the official LaGuardia reading. Minor afternoon convection or localized cloud cover could still shift the exact value by 1–2°F, though current atmospheric stability makes such deviations unlikely before close.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and German Weather Service models show Munich under stable high pressure with southerly flow, supporting daytime maxima of 32–34°C on August 14 with minimal cloud cover and low precipitation probability. Recent model runs have shown little shift in the 48-hour window, reinforcing trader consensus around this narrow range while noting that small changes in boundary-layer moisture or wind could nudge outcomes toward 32°C or 35°C.

This forecast aligns with ensemble model consensus and explains why the 29 °C outcome holds the strongest market-implied probability at 57.5 %. Recent model runs show only modest upside risk if skies clear earlier or downside if heavier rain arrives, keeping 28 °C and 30 °C as secondary possibilities at 26.5 % and 11.5 %. Updated JMA briefings and hourly observations through the afternoon will provide the final data for resolution.

Historical mid-August normals hover near 83°F, so the current setup represents a modest positive anomaly without extreme heat advection. Key uncertainties include the precise timing of peak insolation and any localized afternoon cumulus development; updated NWS short-range guidance and high-resolution model runs expected later today could refine the exact threshold and shift probabilities between the two leading outcomes.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Tokyo's August 15 maximum temperature centers on short-range forecast consensus from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and global models, with 29°C and 30°C leading at 26% and 22% implied probability.** These closely matched odds reflect genuine uncertainty in the final 48-hour window before the event, typical for narrow temperature bins where small shifts in cloud cover, timing of precipitation, or boundary-layer mixing can swing the daily peak by 1–2°C.

Persistent seasonal forcing from a strong Pacific High has kept Japan above normal since early summer, with Tokyo experiencing frequent 30–35°C days amid high humidity that enhances urban heat retention. However, guidance for the 15th specifically indicates possible scattered showers or increased cloudiness, which would cap insolation and limit afternoon heating compared with clearer recent days. Model spreads arise mainly from subtle differences in low-level moisture advection and sea-breeze timing along the Kanto Plain, where the urban heat island can add 1–2°C locally but is modulated by any onshore flow or rainfall.

Resolution hinges on the official JMA observation at the Tokyo station; traders weigh the latest ensemble runs showing a most-likely peak near 29–30°C against the risk of slightly cooler conditions if showers arrive earlier or stronger than expected. This produces the tight clustering around the two leading outcomes while keeping higher tails (31°C+) at low single-digit probabilities.

Historical mid-August normals hover near 83°F, so the current setup represents a modest positive anomaly without extreme heat advection. eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and German Weather Service models show Munich under stable high pressure with southerly flow, supporting daytime maxima of 32–34°C on August 14 with minimal cloud cover and low precipitation probability. These conditions align with the market-implied probabilities favoring 33°C (41%) and 34°C (31%), as historical August climatology in Bavaria rarely exceeds 35°C without stronger advection. Recent model runs have shown little shift in the 48-hour window, reinforcing trader consensus around this narrow range while noting that small changes in boundary-layer moisture or wind could nudge outcomes toward 32°C or 35°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest DWD and ECMWF model runs converge on a Munich daytime maximum near 31 °C, driving the dominant market weighting toward that outcome under a stable high-pressure ridge and southwesterly warm advection. This setup produces a positive temperature anomaly relative to the late-August climatological mean of 24–26 °C. Updated official forecasts and real-time observations from the Deutscher Wetterdienst remain the key near-term data points that could refine the precise peak before daily resolution.

Forecast models show limited cloud cover and light winds, minimizing mixing that could suppress peaks, while regional climatology supports highs several degrees above the ~24–25°C August average when anticyclonic conditions dominate. The 30°C and 32°C brackets trail at lower implied probabilities because slight variations in peak timing or minor model adjustments could shift the exact reading by 1°C, but the consensus range remains tightly clustered around 31°C with little chance of extremes given the absence of stronger advection or precipitation. Updated model runs and station observations through midday will be the key near-term drivers.

**Current Met Office guidance and ensemble model consensus from the Met Office and ECMWF place the maximum temperature in London on August 14 at 33°C, with a narrow spread centered on 32–33°C.** This directly supports the market’s leading outcome at 53.5% implied probability for 33°C, followed by 34°C (24.5%) and 32°C (14.0%).

A persistent high-pressure system over southern England continues to advect warm continental air northward while promoting clear skies and strong solar insolation. These conditions, combined with typical London urban heat-island effects, have sustained daytime maxima near or above 33°C through mid-August. The amber extreme-heat warning and recent peaks of 35°C on August 13 further anchor expectations for only modest overnight cooling before the next day’s heating cycle.

Model spreads remain limited, reflecting stable steering patterns and minimal risk of significant cloud cover or frontal activity on the 14th. Traders therefore assign the bulk of probability mass to the 32–34°C band, consistent with official point forecasts and climatological context for a late-summer heat episode. New model runs or observational updates from the Met Office could refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.
